zh.caseTitle: 案件：「玩手机导致近视」的调查
zh.testimony: 我们的调查覆盖了全市 30 所学校，结果发现：近视的学生平均每天看屏幕的时间明显更长。调查员通过问卷让学生自己填写每天的屏幕使用时长。据此我们认为，长时间玩手机直接导致近视，建议家长严格限制孩子使用电子产品。至于视力正常的学生，他们本来就更爱户外运动，这并不影响我们的结论。

textRefs.spot_crosssection: 近视的学生平均每天看屏幕的时间明显更长
textRefs.spot_selfreport: 调查员通过问卷让学生自己填写每天的屏幕使用时长
textRefs.spot_nocontrol2: 视力正常的学生，他们本来就更爱户外运动，这并不影响我们的结论
textRefs.debunk_crosssection: 横断面研究：同一时间点的相关性无法说明因果方向——也许是近视了才更依赖屏幕，而不是屏幕导致近视。
textRefs.debunk_selfreport: 自报偏差：学生自己报的屏幕时长可能不准确——被家长监督的孩子会少报，问卷数据未必真实。
textRefs.debunk_nocontrol2: 忽略替代解释：视力正常的学生更爱户外运动——运动量、遗传、家庭习惯都是可能的原因，「不影响结论」一句话带过太轻率。
textRefs.q_crosssection: 这是同一时间点的调查吗？能区分「谁先谁后」吗？
textRefs.q_selfreport: 学生自报的时长准确吗？有没有客观测量？
textRefs.q_nocontrol2: 户外运动、遗传、用眼习惯这些因素，考虑了吗？
textRefs.q_d1: 这份问卷覆盖的是一个月，还是一整个学期？
textRefs.q_d2: 问卷是否匿名，以减少学生故意少报使用时长？

nearMissFeedback.q_d1: 更长的调查窗口可能让相关性更稳定，却仍是同一时点的回顾，回答不了谁先谁后。
nearMissFeedback.q_d2: 匿名能减少故意少报，是合理改进；但记忆误差仍在，也没有提供客观屏幕记录。

hints: 同一时间的调查，说不清谁因谁果
「不影响结论」——其他因素真的排除了吗？
zh.explanation: 这份调查用横断面相关推因果，依赖学生自报，还跳过了户外运动等替代解释。延长问卷覆盖期仍不能回答谁先谁后；匿名能减少故意少报，却不能消除记忆误差，方向正确不等于已经击中要害。

en.caseTitle: Case: A Survey Linking "Phone Use and Myopia"
en.testimony: Our survey covered 30 schools across the city and found that myopic students spend noticeably more time on screens per day on average. Surveyors used questionnaires asking students to self-report their daily screen time. Based on this we conclude that prolonged phone use directly causes myopia, and recommend parents strictly limit children's use of electronics. As for students with normal vision, they simply enjoy outdoor activities more — this does not affect our conclusion.

textRefs.spot_crosssection: myopic students spend noticeably more time on screens per day
textRefs.spot_selfreport: Surveyors used questionnaires asking students to self-report their daily screen time
textRefs.spot_nocontrol2: they simply enjoy outdoor activities more — this does not affect our conclusion
textRefs.debunk_crosssection: Cross-sectional study: correlation at one point in time cannot show causal direction — maybe myopic kids rely on screens more, rather than screens causing myopia.
textRefs.debunk_selfreport: Self-report bias: students' self-reported screen time may be inaccurate — kids under parental supervision under-report; questionnaire data may not be truthful.
textRefs.debunk_nocontrol2: Ignoring rival explanations: normal-vision students are more active outdoors — exercise, genetics, and home habits are all possible causes; dismissing them with "does not affect our conclusion" is careless.
textRefs.q_crosssection: Is this a single-point-in-time survey? Can it tell which came first?
textRefs.q_selfreport: Are the self-reported hours accurate? Was there any objective measurement?
textRefs.q_nocontrol2: Were outdoor activity, genetics, and eye-use habits considered?
textRefs.q_d1: Did the questionnaire cover one month or an entire semester?
textRefs.q_d2: Was the survey anonymous to reduce deliberate under-reporting of screen time?

nearMissFeedback.q_d1: A longer survey window may stabilize the correlation, but a retrospective snapshot still cannot establish which came first.
nearMissFeedback.q_d2: Anonymity can reduce deliberate under-reporting, a real improvement, but recall error remains and no objective screen record is added.

hints: A snapshot in time cannot say which caused which
Self-reported data — how reliable is it?
"Does not affect our conclusion" — were other factors really ruled out?
en.explanation: This survey infers causation from a cross-section, relies on self-report, and skips alternatives such as outdoor activity. A longer questionnaire window still cannot establish what came first; anonymity can reduce deliberate under-reporting but not memory error. A better direction is not yet a direct hit.
